# package l2

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec61850/l2"
```

Package l2 is the raw Ethernet layer shared by the IEC 61850 layer-2 protocols: GOOSE (package goose, EtherType 0x88B8) and Sampled Values (package sv, EtherType 0x88BA).

It provides the [Transport](#type-transport) interface with operating-system backends ([Open](#func-open): Linux AF\_PACKET, macOS/BSD BPF), an in-memory [Hub](#type-hub) with fault injection for tests and simulations, and a [Demux](#type-demux) that lets several protocol stacks share one transport, each receiving only its own EtherTypes. [MAC](#type-mac) is the hardware address type used throughout.

The package is pure Go (golang.org/x/sys), without cgo.

### type Demux

```go
type Demux struct {

	// terminal receive error

}
```

Demux shares one [Transport](#type-transport) between several receivers, for example a GOOSE and a Sampled Values subscriber on the same raw socket. A background goroutine receives from the transport and hands each frame to every port registered for its EtherType (one 802.1Q tag is looked through); frames of other EtherTypes are discarded. Sends go straight to the shared transport.

Each port has a bounded queue; when a slow receiver lets it fill up, further frames for that port are dropped and counted in [DemuxStats](#type-demuxstats).Overflow, so one receiver never blocks another.

#### func NewDemux

```go
func NewDemux(t Transport, queue int) *Demux
```

NewDemux starts demultiplexing t. The Demux owns t: [Demux.Close](#func-demux-close) closes it. queue is the per-port queue length; values below 1 mean DefaultDemuxQueue.

#### func (Demux) Close

```go
func (d *Demux) Close() error
```

Close closes the shared transport and every port, and waits for the receive goroutine to stop. It is idempotent.

#### func (Demux) Err

```go
func (d *Demux) Err() error
```

Err returns the receive error that stopped the Demux, ErrClosed after Close, or nil while it is running.

#### func (Demux) Port

```go
func (d *Demux) Port(etherTypes ...uint16) (*DemuxPort, error)
```

Port returns a new [Transport](#type-transport) that receives the frames of the given EtherTypes. Several ports may share an EtherType; each gets every matching frame (frames are shared read-only between ports, so a receiver must not modify a frame it got from Recv). Sending on a port sends on the shared transport. Closing a port detaches it without affecting the others.

#### func (Demux) Stats

```go
func (d *Demux) Stats() DemuxStats
```

Stats returns a snapshot of the counters.

### type Faults

```go
type Faults struct {
	// Loss drops a delivery.
	Loss float64

	// Duplicate delivers a frame twice.
	Duplicate float64

	// Reorder holds a frame back and delivers it after the next frame
	// for the same port.
	Reorder float64

	// Delay postpones every delivery by this duration.
	Delay time.Duration

	// Seed seeds the random source; equal seeds give equal fault
	// sequences for the same traffic.
	Seed int64

	// Mutate, when non-nil, is applied to a private copy of each frame
	// before delivery. Returning nil drops the frame.
	Mutate func(frame []byte) []byte
}
```

Faults configures fault injection on a [Hub](#type-hub). Rates are probabilities in \[0, 1], evaluated independently per delivery.

### type Hub

```go
type Hub struct {

	// reorder: frame held back per port

}
```

Hub is an in-memory Ethernet segment. Every frame sent on one port is delivered to every other port, like a shared bridge. It is intended for tests, simulations and examples; frames never touch the network.

A Hub can inject faults (loss, duplication, reordering, delay and arbitrary mutation) to exercise subscriber supervision. All methods are safe for concurrent use.

### type MAC

```go
type MAC [6]byte
```

MAC is an IEEE 802 48-bit hardware address. The zero value is the all-zero address, which subscriber filters treat as "any".

ParseMAC parses a hardware address written as six hexadecimal octets separated by '-' or ':' (the SCL MAC-Address form is "01-0C-CD-01-00-01") or as twelve contiguous hex digits.

### type Transport

```go
type Transport interface {
	// Send transmits one complete Ethernet frame.
	Send(frame []byte) error

	// Recv blocks until a frame is received, ctx is done (returning
	// ctx.Err()) or the transport is closed (returning [ErrClosed]).
	Recv(ctx context.Context) ([]byte, error)

	// HardwareAddr returns the interface address, used as the default
	// source address by publishers.
	HardwareAddr() MAC

	// Close releases the transport. Blocked Recv calls return
	// [ErrClosed]. Close is idempotent.
	Close() error
}
```

Transport sends and receives raw Ethernet frames (without FCS).

Implementations must be safe for concurrent use: one goroutine may block in Recv while others call Send. Send must not retain frame after it returns. Recv returns a slice owned by the caller.

Backends: [Open](#func-open) (Linux AF\_PACKET, macOS/BSD BPF) and [Hub](#type-hub) (in memory, for tests and simulations). A [Demux](#type-demux) shares one Transport between several receivers.

#### func Open

```go
func Open(iface string, opts TransportOptions) (Transport, error)
```

Open opens a raw Ethernet transport on the named interface using an AF\_PACKET socket. It requires CAP\_NET\_RAW (or root). A kernel socket filter limits delivery to opts.EtherTypes (default GOOSE), untagged or 802.1Q tagged. VLAN tags stripped by NIC offload are restored from PACKET\_AUXDATA so that decoded frames report their VLAN.

### type TransportOptions

```go
type TransportOptions struct {
	// EtherTypes lists the EtherTypes delivered by Recv; a kernel filter
	// drops everything else (untagged or with one 802.1Q tag). Empty
	// means GOOSE only ([EtherTypeGOOSE]), the behaviour of
	// goose.Open; sv.Open passes [EtherTypeSV]. Pass both to receive
	// GOOSE and SV on one socket and split them with a [Demux].
	EtherTypes []uint16

	// Promiscuous puts the interface in promiscuous mode. On macOS/BSD
	// it is required to receive multicast groups that the host has not
	// joined, so [Open] enables it there unless Multicast is non-empty
	// and the platform supports group membership.
	Promiscuous bool

	// Multicast lists destination groups to join. When empty on Linux
	// the socket receives all multicast traffic (PACKET_MR_ALLMULTI).
	Multicast []MAC

	// ReceiveLocal also delivers frames sent from this host by other
	// sockets, so a publisher and a subscriber can run on the same
	// machine. On Linux the transport then also receives its own
	// frames.
	ReceiveLocal bool

	// Logger receives transport diagnostics. Nil disables logging.
	Logger *slog.Logger
}
```

TransportOptions configures a raw Ethernet transport opened with [Open](#func-open).
